Consider the system of equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3y-2z=4 \\ -2x-3y=-6 \\ x+4z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}$, where $D$ is the determinant of the coefficient matrix and ${D}_{y}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}0x+3y+(-2)z=4 \\ (-2)x+(-3)y+0z=-6 \\ 1x+0y+4z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
D=|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}|.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+y-z=1 \\ x-2y+2z=3 \\ 3x-2y+z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $5,$ then $x=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+1y+(-1)z=1 \\ 1x+(-2)y+2z=3 \\ 3x+(-2)y+1z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2-(-4))-(3-4)-(-6-(-4)) \\  & =2+1+2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{5}{5}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y-z=1 \\ 2x-3z=-2 \\ -x+y-2z=6\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $42,$ then $x=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y+(-1)z=1 \\ 2x+0y+(-3)z=-2 \\ (-1)x+1y+(-2)z=6.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|=42.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(0+3)-5(4+18)-(-2-0) \\  & =3-110+2 \\  & =-105.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{-105}{42}=-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-3y+z=5 \\ x+y-2z=-3 \\ -5x+4z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $7,$ then $y=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+(-3)y+1z=5 \\ 1x+1y+(-2)z=-3 \\ -5x+0y+4z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -5 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}|=7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{y},$ we take the coefficients matrix, replace the second column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ -5 & -1 & 4\end{aligned}| & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -5 & 4\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -5 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =5(-12-2)-5(4-10)+(-1-15) \\  & =-70+30-16 \\  & =-56.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{-56}{7}=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y+3z=-2 \\ 2x-y=3 \\ -x-2y+z=6\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-18,$ then $x=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}1x+1y+3z=-2 \\ 2x+(-1)y+0z=3 \\ (-1)x+(-2)y+1z=6.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}|=-18.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(-1-0)-(3-0)-(-6+6) \\  & =2-3-0 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{-1}{-18}=\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+4y+2z=-2 \\ 2x-5y+1z=-10 \\ 2x+y-2z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $66,$ then $y=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+4y+2z=-2 \\ 2x+(-5)y+1z=-10 \\ 2x+1y+(-2)z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|=66\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{y},$ we take the coefficients matrix, replace the second column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & -10 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-10 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}|-(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -10 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(20+1)+2(-4-2)+2(-2+20) \\  & =42-12+36 \\  & =66.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{66}{66}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-3y-z=1 \\ x+4y+kz=-1 \\ 2x+3y+4z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that  $z=1$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $97-21k,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & k \\ 2 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}|=97-21k\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $z$ is given by $z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 9\end{aligned}| & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}|-(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =5(36+3)+3(9+2)+(3-8) \\  & =195+33-5 \\  & =223.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{223}{97-21k}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $z=1.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{223}{97-21k} & =1 \\ 223 & =97-21k \\ 21k & =-126 \\ k & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}6x+5y-3z=2 \\ 4x-5y+kz=1 \\ -2x+10y-5z=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that  $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $160-70k,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & -2 \\ 4 & -5 & k \\ -2 & 10 & -5\end{aligned}|=160-70k\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -5 & k \\ -2 & 10 & -5\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-5 & k \\ 10 & -5\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & k \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}|+(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -2 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(25-10k)-5(-5+2k)-3(10-10) \\  & =50-20k+25-10k+0 \\  & =75-30k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{75-30k}{160-70k}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{75-30k}{160-70k} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ 2(75-30k) & =160-70k \\ 150-60k & =160-70k \\ 10k & =10 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+3y+z=3 \\ x-z=k \\ x-2y+2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $z=2$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-15,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}|=-15\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $z$ is given by $z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & k \\ 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & k \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & k \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(0+2k)-3(1-k)+3(-2-0) \\  & =4k-3+3k-6 \\  & =7k-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{7k-9}{-15}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $z=2.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7k-9}{-15} & =2 \\ 7k-9 & =-30 \\ 7k & =-21 \\ k & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y+2z=6 \\ 3x+2y-z=k \\ 4x+3y-3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $x=1$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-9,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}|=-9\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 2 \\ k & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}| & =6\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =6(-6+3)+(-3k+1)+2(3k-2) \\  & =-18-3k+1+6k-4 \\  & =3k-21.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{3k-21}{-9}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $x=1.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-9}{3k-21} & =1 \\ -9 & =3k-21 \\ 12 & =3k \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+3y+2z=k \\ x+y=-1 \\ y+z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $y=-5$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $1,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}|=1\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}2 & k & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|-k\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1-0)-k(1-0)+2(2-0) \\  & =-2-k+4 \\  & =2-k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{2-k}{1}=2-k.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $y=-5.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-k & =-5 \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\langle x,y,z \rangle$ be the solution of the system of equations below. Find $z.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=-1 \\ 4x-2z=1 \\ 3x+y-z=-2\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}1x-1y+3z=-1 \\ 4x+0y-2z=1 \\ 3x+1y-1z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

We start by finding the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(0-(-2))+(-4+6)+3(4-0) \\  & =2+2+12 \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find $D_z,$ we take the coefficients matrix, replace the *third* column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(0-1)+(-8-3)-(4-0) \\  & =-1-11-4 \\  & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{-16}{16}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ k & 3 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(6-2)-2(2k+6)-(-k-9) \\  & =4-4k-12+k+9 \\  & =1-3k\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x = \dfrac{D_x}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(6-2)-2(2+6)-(-1-9) \\  & =-4-16+10 \\  & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
x = \dfrac{D_x}{D} = \dfrac{-10}{1-3k}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $x=2.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-10}{1-3k} & =2 \\ -10 & =2-6k \\ 6k & =12 \\ k & =2\end{aligned}
$$
